title: Verify edited-submission detection in the existing incremental-sync PR
problem: Issue #7259 reports that API consumers must re-download and compare entire submission collections to detect edits. Existing PR #7260 implements a modified-time field; Humanifest should investigate verification gaps and support its author, not open a replacement.
humanitarian_relevance: Correct incremental updates could reduce repeated data transfer and keep humanitarian analysis current. The reported workload is one user's account, not an independently measured platform-wide compute saving.

evidence.claim: The issue author reports nightly replication of about 35 forms and 230,000 submissions to detect roughly 0.1% changed records. No Humanifest benchmark verifies those figures or achievable savings.
A second commenter says the feature is needed for their project and points to the existing PR. This is demand evidence, not maintainer approval.

On 2026-09-08 the issue timeline links open PR #7260 by another contributor. The public PR description identifies tests and a remaining API-schema documentation question; its automated review is not independent validation.

code_surface: Issue points to kobo/apps/openrosa/apps/viewer/models/parsed_instance.py and logger/utils/instance.py. PR description names viewer/tests/test_date_modified.py and API schema documentation. PR diff and actual test contents still need pinned inspection.
proposed_change: Research now: pin the current PR #7260 head, read its diff and existing tests, and build an evidence matrix for ordinary edits, bulk validation changes, attachment-only changes, legacy records and incremental-query boundaries. Identify only uncovered behaviors or documentation gaps; coordinate with the existing author before proposing additions. Do not send an unsolicited automated PR review.
tests: Compare the author's tests with the update-path matrix. Plan synthetic checks for timestamp monotonicity, equal-time pagination boundaries, legacy fallback/query consistency and unchanged exports. These are investigation questions, not established defects or executed tests.
environment: Tier 0 public source/API inspection only. No target clone, dependency install, setup, test, or production write. Inspect manifests, hooks, services and secrets before any execution.
maintainer: Research can proceed independently now. Confirm the specific scope and whether support is wanted before implementation or outbound review.
risks: Initial intake is not implementation readiness. Preserve existing contributors, avoid production data, and verify policy and scope before publishing target work.
priority_rationale: Second new investigation, across a different maintainer team: two public users describe incremental-sync need, and an existing author has provided a patch. Independent gap analysis could reduce review burden without duplicating implementation.
